dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Sandra. Good morning, how can I help you?
Good morning, Sandra, thank you for taking my call. My name is Rui Silva. I am calling about a noise problem, if that is the right office. Thank you.
Well, you're in the right place to start, hon. Noise, okay. What's going on?
So, my neighbor plays very loud music every weekend. Friday night, Saturday, sometimes into Sunday. It has been going on the better part of a month now. Thank you for listening.
A whole month of weekends, oh, that wears on you. Is it a party kind of thing or just the stereo going?

It is the stereo, I think, with a lot of bass. I can feel it in the floor of my living room. This past weekend, with the nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, I was home both days because of the weather. I could not get away from it. I thought the storm would keep them quiet, but no, it did not.
You'd think the wind would drown it out. No luck, huh?

No, unfortunately not. It is the same thing each time, and I have asked nicely once at the door. It did not change anything. So I am calling to ask, please, what are the quiet hours in Newport? Thank you.

Good question. Generally the city has nighttime quiet hours, late evening through early morning, and loud music that carries to the neighbors can be a problem at any hour if it's unreasonable. I don't want to read you the exact hours off the top of my head and get a minute wrong. Let me see if I can pull it up.
Of course. Take your time, please. I am in no rush. Thank you.
Bless you. Hold on one second.
Certainly.

[pause] Okay, I'm back. So the noise ordinance is something enforced by the police department, not by us here at the clerk's office. For something that keeps happening on weekend nights, you'd call their non-emergency line while it's actually going on, so an officer can hear it.
I see. So I should call while the music is playing. Not afterward. Is that right? Thank you.
Right, that's the way. If you call Monday morning, there's nothing for them to witness. And if it's every weekend, a log of dates and times helps too.
A log. Yes, I can do that. I have actually been writing down the dates already, on the back of an envelope. I will make it a proper list. Thank you for the suggestion.
There you go, you're ahead of the game. Do you know if the neighbor owns or rents? Not that you have to say, just curious if there's a landlord involved.

I am not certain. I believe it may be a rental, but I would not want to say something wrong. I am the homeowner on my side, so I would like to keep a good relationship if possible. But it is getting hard. Honestly, it is very frustrating, Sandra. Every weekend, again, and nothing changes.
I hear you. A month is a long time to put up with it, and you did try the polite way first. That counts for something.
Thank you. I did try. I thought that would be enough.
Some folks just don't realize how it carries. Sometimes a second conversation or a note helps, but if the bass is shaking your floor, calling it in is perfectly fair.

Yes, I think so too. Oh, one moment, please. I am sorry. I stopped on the way to buy a lottery scratch ticket and I have not scratched it yet. It is sitting here on the table next to me. I keep looking at it. Excuse me.
Well, don't let me stop you. Maybe it's your lucky day and you can buy a house with thick walls.
I will wait until after the call. It would not be polite to scratch during. Thank you. So, to confirm, the police non-emergency line, during the noise, and keep a list of dates.

That's it exactly. And if it keeps up after that, you can come back to us or write to the city and we'll point you to the right person. Do you want me to note your name and number in case someone follows up?
Yes, please, that would be kind. My name is Rui Silva, and the number is 401-555-0190. Thank you.
Got it, Rui Silva, 401-555-0190. I'll make a note of the complaint. No promises on a call back, but it's on record.
I understand. Thank you very much, Sandra. I appreciate your help today.
Anytime. Hang in there, and good luck with the ticket.
Thank you. Have a good day. Goodbye.
